styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey cast-iron stand. It has a lighter top plane, mid and dark body faces, and a darker base, which reads as about 5 value steps on the iron. The measured facts support this: 17 distinct colours packed into the tile (the median per tile is also 17, equal to the stall and close to the well), 0% 5x5 flat-fill coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. So the outline is tinted to the material, not a neutral black sticker line. Its 17 total colours are above the bench, hedge and lamp (11-14) and below the larger stall and well (38-40), which is reasonable for a one-tile prop. Texture is modest, with some speckle and panel detail on the iron face, and it looks less textured than the stall or well. At this size it would sit acceptably next to the references without looking flatter or more sticker-like, so it passes.
